# traceforce Provider

Manages Traceforce resources.

## Authentication

Log in one of two ways:

- `api_key` (or `TRACEFORCE_API_KEY`): an API key.
- `client_id` + `client_secret` (or `TRACEFORCE_CLIENT_ID` + `TRACEFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET`): one of your Traceforce API clients (Settings → API Clients). The provider gets a token at every run. `device_id` (or `TRACEFORCE_DEVICE_ID`) says who the token is for, e.g. `cloud-collector-aws` for the cloud collector.

A value in the provider block wins over its environment variable, also across the two ways: a configured `api_key` is used even when `TRACEFORCE_CLIENT_ID` is exported. Both ways at the same level (both in the provider block, or `TRACEFORCE_API_KEY` and `TRACEFORCE_CLIENT_ID` both in the environment) is an error, "Two Traceforce logins": unset one, or set the one to use in the provider block.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Log in with an API key ...
provider "traceforce" {
  endpoint = "https://your-traceforce-endpoint.traceforce.ai/v1"
  api_key  = "your-api-key-here"
}

# ... or with one of your API clients (Settings -> API Clients), e.g. the cloud collector:
# provider "traceforce" {
#   endpoint      = "https://your-traceforce-endpoint.traceforce.ai/v1"
#   client_id     = var.traceforce_client_id
#   client_secret = var.traceforce_client_secret
#   device_id     = "cloud-collector-aws"
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String) API key to the service. Or `TRACEFORCE_API_KEY`.
- `client_id` (String) Client ID of an API client, used instead of `api_key`. Or `TRACEFORCE_CLIENT_ID`.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client secret of that API client. Or `TRACEFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
- `device_id` (String) Who the token is for when logging in with `client_id`, e.g. `cloud-collector-aws`. Or `TRACEFORCE_DEVICE_ID`.
- `endpoint` (String) Service endpoint. Or `TRACEFORCE_ENDPOINT`.
- `extra_headers` (Map of String) Additional headers to include in API requests
